newsitem.title: PERU: Peru and Ecuador leaders talk peace in Lima.
newsitem.headline: Peru and Ecuador leaders talk peace in Lima.

text.p: The presidents of Peru and Ecuador -- two Andean nations still at odds over a decades-old border dispute -- hugged each other on Monday and pledged to work together for peace during an historic meeting in Lima.

Peruvian President Alberto Fujimori hailed the arrival of his Ecuador(e)an counterpart Abdala Bucaram for a three-day visit as "a gigantic step ... which augurs a common horizon with enormous possibilities."

An effusive Bucaram, on the first official bilateral visit by an Ecuador(e)an president to Peru, proclaimed his "profound satisfaction and intense happiness ... because I have found a fraternal people who shout with passion and fervor 'peace, peace, peace'."

The visit was intended to aid peace talks between the two nations over a bitter 55-year-old territorial dispute that has caused regular armed clashes, including a short January 1995 war that left dozens dead and hundreds injured on both sides.
Fujimori also used the visit to show that his country's affairs were going on as usual despite the 27-day hostage crisis at the Japanese ambassador's residence.

Marxist rebels from the Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement were quick to respond to Bucaram's visit, putting a sign in a window of the house reading: "The fraternal peoples of Peru and Ecuador wish for peace with social justice".

Fujimori took Bucaram -- and a chaotic caravan of journalists and officials -- on a tour of Lima shantytowns where crowds lined the streets with Peruvian and Ecuador(e)an flags, shouting "Peace, peace, we want peace."

At one point Bucaram stepped out of his black Mercedes, only to be lifted onto the shoulders of the crowd. But the Ecuador(e)an president, who recently launched an album of his rock music, declined the crowd's entreaties to sing to them.
The two countries signed four low-level cooperation agreements at Government Palace covering health, education, natural disasters and cultural heritage.
"We are faithful interpreters of the desire for peace and cooperation felt by the peoples of Peru and Ecuador in their overwhelming majorities," Bucaram said.
"'The Chinaman' and 'The Madman' are going to make peace in America," he added, referring to each presidents' popular nickname.
